name: Downes v. Bidwell
summary: The Supreme Court held that Puerto Rico, as an unincorporated territory, was not fully subject to all provisions of the U.S. Constitution, establishing the contested doctrine that territories occupy a different legal status than states.
significance: This is one of the foundational 'Insular Cases' establishing that the Constitution does not automatically apply in full to U.S. territories, which is central to the dispute over whether NEPA's requirements apply equally to Guam.
